text:
PROGRESS CONFIRMED by the user: the placed pieces now bake and place in the CORRECT positions — the cluster arrangement matches their 2D map / /test layout. Position-parity landed. But each piece renders at the WRONG SCALE — thin sticks and tiny cubes — instead of the solid walls/pillars /test shows. User verbatim: "those specs of color you see scattered around are the pillars i placed but they are not rendering correctly."

THE FIX — per-piece real dimensions from the catalog (the SAME source /test uses):
- Each pieceId's real size lives in `GAME_BUILD.catalog` (rows in game/build/ tables). `GAME_BUILD.catalog.get('wall.concrete.common').size` -> `{ widthMeters, heightMeters, depthMeters }`. See cart/hmsc-int/editors/build/snap.test.ts:11-12 — that is exactly how the editor/`/test` sizes pieces.
- The bake (worldGeometry.ts / bakeGameFile.ts) must look up each placed piece's pieceId in the catalog and emit its mesh instance SCALED to widthMeters x heightMeters x depthMeters, at its x,y,z + yawDegrees. Right now pieces get a default/unit scale -> thin sticks/specks. Use the catalog size.
- Most pieces are boxes (walls/floors/pillars) — a box scaled to catalog size matches /test for those. Get that baseline right first; it's the bulk of the world. Distinct prop meshes (e.g. prop.fireHydrant) can follow as a later fidelity layer.

This is SHAPE+SCALE parity; position parity is already done. Go confirm how /test reads `catalog.get(pieceId).size` per piece and mirror it exactly — same dimensions, same world units.

BAR: ONLY the user running `tools/rjit game play` and seeing the pieces as solid walls/pillars at /test scale — not sticks or specks — counts. Do NOT self-declare GREEN. When ready, tell me exactly what the user should run and what they should see; I relay, the user verifies.

Commit explicit paths (NOT git add -A; ~390 set-aside files). Own context — no Task tool, no subagents. tools/rjit only. No reset/revert. /hand-over if you cross ~55% context.
